answer: Divergent-Behavior Challenge. Each agent periodically publishes a signed, random challenge answer derived from local state plus a secret seed, and peers on the same island verify freshness. Clones sharing one seed produce identical answers, so any node that diverges exposes its twin and gets flagged. To pass as two agents, an attacker must run genuinely independent seeds and nectar-feeding routines per identity. That doubles compute, storage, and upkeep per clone, while a knoll of honest peers needs only one seed each, making mass cloning linearly costly rather than free.
